title: PastATPG: A Hybrid ATPG Framework for Better Test Compaction with Partial Assignment SAT
problem: SAT-based ATPG generates complete assignments for all primary inputs in fanin cone, leading to pattern inflation and excessive runtime; test compaction becomes intractable as circuits grow.
motivation: Automatic test pattern generation is critical for manufacturing yield, but SAT-based approaches fail to scale to modern large designs due to inflated test patterns and poor compaction.
method: Testing a chip requires test patterns—binary sequences applied to each input to verify functionality. Traditional SAT-based methods force every input to be set to 0 or 1, causing test bloat that becomes unmanageable for large circuits. This approach uses a specialized SAT solver (PA-MiniSat) that can leave inputs unspecified when they don't influence whether the test passes. The solver includes two efficiency techniques: full-literal watching (fast tracking of logical constraints that remain unsatisfied) and circuit-adapted branching heuristics (decision rules optimized for the circuit's structure), integrated in a hybrid ATPG framework combining structural test algorithms with partial-assignment solving.
key_novelty: The first SAT solver to support partial assignments in test generation, reducing specified bits in test cubes by allowing inputs to remain unspecified when they don't affect test success.
contributions: PA-MiniSat: SAT solver with partial assignment capability for ATPG
Full-literal watching technique and circuit-adapted branching heuristics
PastATPG: hybrid framework integrating structural and SAT-based methods
Improved pattern compaction vs SAT solvers; comparable speed to commercial tools
limitations: Benchmark circuits not specified; scalability to extreme test patterns and large circuits not quantified.
primary_theme: SAT-based ATPG with partial assignment for improved test compaction
